_comment: USG RADIUS - Proxy with an upstream RadSec (RFC 6614) home server
_description: NASes reach this proxy over plain UDP RADIUS with per-client secrets; requests for the realm are forwarded to a home server over one persistent, mutually authenticated TLS 1.3 connection (ML-KEM-1024-only key exchange, AES-256-GCM-SHA384). Health probes (RFC 5997 Status-Server) run over the same connection.
_transport_notes: The proxy is active only when the NAS hop is `transport: udp-insecure`: under the inbound `radsec` listener the server runs the RadSec accept loop and does not start the proxy components.

Per home server, `transport` is `udp` (default; `secret` required) or `radsec` (`tls` block required; `secret` must be absent — RFC 6614 §2.3 fixes the hop secret to the string "radsec", and the TLS certificates are what authenticate the hop).

`tls.server_name` is the DNS name or IP literal the home server's certificate must be valid for; it is also sent as SNI. The link verifies the certificate chain against `tls.ca_path` and never falls back to UDP.

`tls.revocation` is the same block as `eap.tls.revocation` / `radsec.revocation` and checks the home server's certificate for revocation (needs a binary built with the `revocation` feature); see examples/proxy_config.json for a static-CRL example.
While the link is down, forwarded requests wait in the proxy cache and the retry manager resends them; after `retry.max_retries` the NAS receives a signed Access-Reject.

`health_check.enabled` must be true when any home server uses `radsec`: the RFC 5997 Status-Server probe is the RFC 6613 §2.6 watchdog of the connection (two unanswered probes reset it), and `health_check.interval` should stay below the home server's TLS idle timeout so the connection stays warm.
`max_outstanding` is at most 255 per RadSec home server (RFC 6613 §2.6.5: one Identifier space per connection, one Identifier kept free for the watchdog).
